title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Renewal Premium and Remittance Calculation
content:
### Renewal premium of the coming term — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

**Scope.** For a renewal remittance the insured makes before the term end on a policy on a tier that carries no ICC coverage, and only for such a remittance, the risk premium of the renewed term follows the cap rule of this schedule and the Federal Policy Fee of the coming term is the fee rated on the policy; every other renewal keeps the base rule: the risk premium booked for the renewed term is the lower of the indicated premium and the prior term's rated risk premium increased by the tier's annual risk premium increase cap, rounded to the cent; the ICC premium and Federal Policy Fee are the engine's figures for the coming term.

**Indicated premium.** The indicated premium is the one on the renewal bill for the term that starts on this policy's term end, the most recently issued such bill.

**Residence basis.** The coming term is rated as the insured's primary residence when the tier can carry the lower surcharge and the policy carries the insured's primary-residence designation, the designation being the record of the residence documentation the insured gave.

**Annual cap percentage.** 18 percent when the coming term is rated as the insured's primary residence and 25 percent otherwise, as the statutory limits for those categories set it.

**Cap rule.** The capped amount is the rated risk premium increased by the annual cap percentage and rounded half-up to the cent, and the renewed risk premium is the lower of the indicated premium and the capped amount.

**Term surcharges.**

| Rated as the insured's primary residence | Community on probation | Term surcharges |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | The tier's primary-residence HFIAA surcharge and the probation surcharge |
| Yes | No | The primary-residence HFIAA surcharge alone |
| No | Yes | The other HFIAA surcharge and the probation surcharge |
| No | No | The other HFIAA surcharge |

**Renewal premium.** The renewal premium is the sum of the coming term's components: the renewed risk premium, the reserve fund assessment (the tier's Reserve Fund Assessment percentage of the renewed risk premium, rounded half-up to the cent), the term surcharges and the Federal Policy Fee rated on the policy.

**Remittance.** The standard remittance is the coming term's premium alone. The remittance is the renewal premium adjusted as the rules of this schedule give, in this order: adjustments first, then limits, then the credits booked with the remittance, rounded half-up to the cent (a half cent, within a tolerance of 0.0001 cent, goes to the higher cent).

**Hypothetical worked example** (invented figures). A policy not rated as a primary residence, community not on probation; rated risk premium 1,000.00 dollars; indicated premium 1,300.00 dollars; rated Federal Policy Fee 50.00 dollars; a tier whose other HFIAA surcharge is 250.00 and whose assessment percentage is 18 percent. Capped amount: 1,000.00 increased by 25 percent, 1,250.00; renewed risk premium: the lower of 1,300.00 and 1,250.00, that is 1,250.00; reserve fund assessment 225.00; renewal premium 1,250.00 and 225.00 and 250.00 and 50.00 together, 1,775.00, which is the remittance.
